verification_note: CMake is NOT available in this environment (playbook-confirmed toolchain gap: 'java, node/npm, go, cargo, cmake, mvn' are all absent). Every disposition below is derived from reading the actual C++ header/source files and the real CMakeLists.txt build scripts at the pinned source_revision, not from a build or ctest run -- a materially shallower verification depth than the sibling .NET repository in this same portfolio batch, where dotnet was available and real execution caught a genuine test-suite defect. idea.md's CS1929 MultipartParser.SequenceEqualAscii claim is specific to the .NET repository's C# receiver-type system and has no direct C++ analogue (there is no equivalent language feature to misuse the same way); this repository's own multipart-splitting logic (src/msg/mime/mime_reader.cpp, internal, not part of the public API surface) was read directly and appears structurally sound, but was not compiled or executed, so it is not asserted as SUPPORTED beyond what reading alone establishes.
method: Live GitHub Contents/Trees API reads (gh CLI, authenticated). Read the top-level CMakeLists.txt, tests/CMakeLists.txt, every public header under include/aspose/email/foss/**/*.hpp (26 files), and src/msg/mime/mime_reader.cpp/.hpp (internal MIME parsing, read for context only, not claimed as independently verified).

facts.claim: MSG/EML interoperability: save_to_eml()/load_from_eml() round-trip through the library's own MIME engine, including multipart messages with attachments
facts.evidence: Read src/msg/mime/mime_reader.cpp's parse_entity() boundary-splitting loop directly: it locates each `--boundary` occurrence by linear std::string::find, extracts content between consecutive boundary positions, and detects the closing `--boundary--` via an explicit std::string::compare check -- the logic appears structurally correct on inspection (traced through by hand for a 2-part multipart/related body), but was not compiled or executed (no CMake/C++ toolchain available in this environment), so it is left UNVERIFIED rather than asserted SUPPORTED. This mirrors the .NET sibling repository's equivalent code path (MultipartParser.cs), which WAS executed this session and found accurate aside from one unrelated test-fixture issue -- the C++ logic was not independently exercised to the same depth and should not be assumed to share that same clean result without its own execution-based check.
